transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You multiplied speed by time, but the units don't match—what unit is the speed in, and what unit should it be for this calculation?
d equals vt. I plugged in v and t, so its right. 360 m sounds reasonable for a car.
Okay, let me think.
You're right that distance equals speed times time, but the units must match. Speed in km/h and time in seconds won't work together. What unit should time be in to match km/h?
Why wont they work? Numbers are numbers. 72 times 5 is 360 no matter what.
Good question. One moment.
Numbers need matching units to make sense. For example, if you walk 5 km in 1 hour, you can't multiply 5 by 1 if the time is in minutes. What unit should 5.0 seconds be in to match km/h?
Hours I guess, but whatever. 360 m in 5 seconds seems fine for a fast car. Why is it wrong?
Let me see.
Units must match to make sense. For example, if you walk 6 km in 1 hour, you can't multiply 6 by 60 minutes. What unit should time be in to match km/h?
I just said hours. You havent told me why 360 m is actually wrong though.
Got it. Give me a second.
Units must match to make sense. For example, if you go 60 km in 1 hour, you can't use minutes. What unit should time be in to match km/h?
Hours. Hours. Youre asking the same thing. My answer is still 360 m.
Okay, let me think.
You're right that units must match, but 72 km/h and 5.0 seconds don't match. To make them match, convert km/h to m/s. Try converting 72 km/h to m/s.
Fine, how? And even if I do, wont I get the same kind of answer?
Good question. One moment.
To match km/h with seconds, convert km/h to m/s. For example, 36 km/h is 10 m/s. Try converting 72 km/h to m/s.
So 72 is double, 20 m/s. Then 20 times 5 is 100 m. Oh, thats way different from 360.
Let me see.
You're right that 72 km/h is 20 m/s, and 20 times 5 is 100 m. That's the correct distance.
Okay, so convert to m/s first, d is 100 m. Got it.
